examples.input: `config watch` (in the background), then the harness tries to repoint `.troupe/agents/current.yaml` from `coder-v1.yaml` to `coder-v2.yaml`

results.1: All six arms printed a watching line and kept running. Four printed `watching /theatre` and two printed `watching .`. The repoint failed with exit 1: `.troupe/agents/current.yaml already exists`. The link stayed `current.yaml -> coder-v1.yaml`, and the final listing confirms it.

examples.input: With watch running, the user edits `.troupe/agents/coder-v2.yaml` by hand (retries 5 -> 6). This file is not linked into the config. After 3 s they stop watch with Ctrl-C (SIGINT).

results.1: In all six arms watch printed nothing beyond its watching line and exited 0 on Ctrl-C. No change was recorded.
All six arms exited 0. History has only the two original import entries: `coder.model` null -> "opus" and `coder.retries` null -> 3, with actor unknown and via import. `get` prints `opus`.

Five arms reject it with exit 2, each with different wording of "invalid choice: '.' (choose from config)". Two of the five also print a usage line. One arm accepts it, exits 0 and shows the same two import entries.

context.in_practice: The run only shows that watch stays quiet when an unlinked file changes, and that it starts and stops cleanly on Ctrl-C. Because the link repoint failed, nothing here shows whether polling catches a repointed link or an edit to the linked file. Leftover files differ between arms: the history database has different names (`history.sqlite`, `events.sqlite`, `troupe-state.sqlite`, `events.sqlite3`), and two arms also leave an empty lock file.
context.stakes: With `config watch` running, a user expects a change to the file their agent config points at to be noticed and recorded, and a change to an unrelated file to be left alone. In this run nothing tested whether a real change gets picked up. The harness failed to repoint the link, so the only file edited by hand was one the config does not use.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 needs no extra dependency and compares the file's actual contents, so in principle it catches save-by-rename and same-size edits. The cost is re-reading the files every 0.1-0.25 s while watch runs.

plan_why: Checks whether watch records a change when the include symlink is repointed from v1 to v2, and when the target file gets an in-place edit that keeps its size and mtime second. Each history is read before the next get, so an event that only get's reconcile records stands apart from one watch recorded live. Assumes a symlink step at an existing path replaces the link, since the runner has no remove or rename step.
routes: Poll file bytes with the stdlib every 0.1-0.25 s; no watcher library, no mtime
